selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the passage?
questions.answer: It warns about two major causes of doubt in faith in this age and explains how to be protected from them.

questions.question: How many major helps for escaping the first abyss are explained in this passage?
questions.answer: Two major helps are explained.

questions.question: What is the first matter mainly arguing?
questions.answer: It argues that proof has real force, while denial in general matters is weak.

questions.question: What example is used to show the strength of proof over denial?
questions.answer: The passage uses the example of seeing the new moon at the start of Ramadan.

questions.question: Why does simple non-observation not amount to proof of absence?
questions.answer: Because not seeing something may come from one’s own limitation rather than the thing’s nonexistence.

questions.question: Why does denial remain isolated even when many people repeat it?
questions.answer: Because each person is only expressing a separate lack of perception.

questions.question: What mistake do deniers make when they judge only by themselves?
questions.answer: They confuse their own lack of seeing with the claim that the thing is not real at all.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about human ability to make such an absolute denial?
questions.answer: It implies that human beings are not able to make that kind of complete judgement honestly.

questions.question: What is the basic takeaway of the first short summary?
questions.answer: Positive testimony gathers into one strong line, but denials split into separate lines that do not unite.

questions.question: What two major faith-related problems does this passage begin to address?
questions.answer: It begins to address two deep sources of doubt that disturb certainty in belief.

questions.question: Why does the passage still continue the discussion if that proof already exists elsewhere?
questions.answer: Because it wants to highlight two major sources of hesitation that disturb faith in the present age.

questions.question: What lesson stands at the center of the first matter?
questions.answer: The central lesson is that denial is weak when clear proof is present.

questions.question: In that example, why does not seeing the moon fail to cancel the testimony of those who saw it?
questions.answer: Because failing to see something is not the same as proving it was not there.

questions.question: Why do affirming statements naturally gather strength?
questions.answer: Because they point to one shared reality and so support each other.

questions.question: How does the passage explain the heavy burden on someone trying to prove nonexistence?
questions.answer: It says such a person would need total knowledge covering the whole world and all ages.

questions.question: What is wrong with saying, “I do not see it, so it is not really there”?
questions.answer: That turns a personal limitation into a claim about reality, which is not justified.

questions.question: Why can such personal denial not become a final judgement about reality?
questions.answer: Because private perception cannot cover all that is real.

questions.question: What contrast between affirmation and negation is emphasized in the first summary?
questions.answer: Affirmation gathers into one shared conclusion, while negation breaks into many private conclusions.

questions.question: What overall issue is the passage concerned with?
questions.answer: It is concerned with protecting certainty of faith from doubts and denials.

questions.question: How much of the larger subject does this passage say it will cover?
questions.answer: It says it will mention only part of the issue, focusing on two deep causes of hesitation.

questions.question: In the first matter, how is proof compared with denial in general issues?
questions.answer: Proof is strong and meaningful, while denial is weak and carries little value against clear evidence.

questions.question: In that example, whose statement carries stronger weight and why?
questions.answer: The statement of those who saw the moon carries stronger weight because it rests on direct witness.

questions.question: What happens when one person who affirms is joined by another who points to the same truth?
questions.answer: Their statements become mutually supporting and stronger.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is difficult about proving that something does not exist anywhere?
questions.answer: It would require searching everywhere and across all times, which is far harder than showing that something exists.
